questions.q: In "What makes an online session work Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: List three online sessions you attended. Note what worked and what annoyed you (sound, late start, no captions, too many slides).
Compare the three sessions: start delay, drop-outs, scores.
Take the 10-question check. Pass mark is 70% (draft).
Fix what you learned, then host sessions two and three with a larger or less familiar group.

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Survey scores out of 5: sound 4.4, content 4.6, pace 4.0.
Each learner reads their one-page plan aloud (3 minutes).
Compare the three sessions: start delay, drop-outs, scores.

questions.q: In "Prepare the room and the tech Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Peers watch a recording you are allowed to share (or notes) and give feedback on pace, clarity and inclusion.
Recording consent: say clearly before you record, give people a way to opt out of camera or recording, keep the file private, delete after a stated time.
Compare the three sessions: start delay, drop-outs, scores.
Test sound first: a headset beats a laptop microphone. Check light on your face, background and camera height.

questions.q: In "Audio and video set-up, accessibility and recording consent Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Test the tool: sharing screen, chat, hand-raising, breakout rooms, captions.
Rewrite your run sheet and checklists.
Accessibility: turn captions on, share slides in advance, use readable fonts and contrast, describe visuals aloud, give breaks, allow chat questions.
Write three lessons learned and one decision: offer hosting as a service, practise more, or stay as a participant skill.

questions.q: In "Host three sessions Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Host session one with a small friendly group. Use a co-host to watch the chat and the clock.
